headline.purpose: Section headings; the closing band runs it up to 4.6rem.

title.purpose: Card and step headings, FAQ summaries, app empty-state titles.

label.purpose: Uppercase Example badge, group labels inside product UI, app panel headings. Never a kicker above another heading.

hand.purpose: Caveat Brush callouts beside hand-drawn arrows, short notes, signatures.

shadows.name: ledge

shadows.name: lift

components.css: .ds-code { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; height: 52px; padding: 0 4px 0 16px; border: 2px solid #dfe7e2; border-radius: 14px; background: #ffffff; box-shadow: 0 4px 0 #dfe7e2; } .ds-code:focus-within { border-color: #0a100d; } .ds-code input { width: 9.5ch; border: 0; outline: 0; background: transparent; color: #0a100d; font: 700 1.05rem/1 'Lexend Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-code input::placeholder { letter-spacing: 0.02em; text-transform: none; font-weight: 500; color: #5a6760; } .ds-code button { height: 40px; padding: 0 14px; border: 0; border-radius: 10px; background: #0a100d; color: #ffffff; font: 700 0.92rem/1 'Figtree Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 120ms ease-out; } .ds-code button:active { transform: scale(0.96); } .ds-code button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #2a9a4b; outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview:
A cairn is a stack of stones hikers leave to show the way and prove someone passed. Cairn's interface works the same way: bright, flat shapes stacked into friendly figures, each one a marker of real work a student did. The world is a white page with near-black ink, five fixed colors laid down as solid geometric tiles, and a cast of grainy rock people with faces, limbs and school props. It borrows the familiar education-site arrangement (split hero, proof band, how it works, audiences, story, close) and holds it to Duolingo and Khan Academy craft: chunky pressable buttons, heavy rounded display type, generous air, and color used in big confident fields rather than thin accents.

Density is relaxed on the landing page and moderate in the app, where the same tokens run quieter: green actions, sage-washed surfaces, periwinkle and teal as role markers, rock art saved for empty states and moments of success. Light and dark are both first-class. Dark mode keeps the palette and swaps the ground for a deep green-black, never a neutral gray.

The system refuses the dark, chat-window look of AI tools and anything that reads as surveillance: no monitoring dashboards, no warning reds as decoration, no cold neutral grays.
keyCharacteristics: Five fixed brand colors with fixed roles; neutrals lean green so they belong to the ink.
Heavy geometric display face (Lexend, 800) over a friendly humanist body (Figtree).
Solid shape tiles (half-discs, quarter circles, D-shapes, rings) as the structural ornament.
Flat rock characters with a grain filter, faces, arms, legs and props.
Sparkles, squiggle underlines and hand-drawn arrows with Caveat Brush notes.
Pressable primary actions with a 4px ledge underneath, Duolingo style.

rules.name: The Five Stones Rule
rules.body: The five brand colors are fixed. New surfaces get color by role (green acts, mint marks good news, periwinkle is students, teal is teachers, ink grounds), never by inventing a sixth hue.

rules.name: The Ink-On-Color Rule
rules.body: Text on green, mint, periwinkle and teal is ink. White text appears only on ink, and on the darker member-avatar shades.

rules.name: The Green-Leaning Neutral Rule
rules.body: No neutral gray. Every gray in the system is tinted toward the ink's green.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: No eyebrow or kicker label sits above a heading. The heading opens its section by itself; a squiggle underline may follow it.

rules.name: The Highlighter Rule
rules.body: Emphasis inside long text is a mint highlighter swipe across the lower half of the line (same size, same weight), never a large pull quote. In dark mode the swipe drops to mint at 32% opacity.

rules.name: The Ledge Is For Pressing Rule
rules.body: The 4px ledge belongs only to things you press (primary buttons, the code field). Cards, tiles and badges never get a hard offset shadow.

rules.name: The Flat Grainy People Rule
rules.body: Characters are flat rock people with grain, faces and limbs, in brand colors only. No gradients, no glossy 3D, no photo people.

dos: Do give every color a role: green acts, mint marks good news, periwinkle is students, teal is teachers.
Do put ink text on every brand color fill.
Do use Lexend 800 with tight tracking (-0.03em to -0.04em) for headlines and Figtree for everything you read.
Do mark emphasis in long text with the mint highlighter swipe.
Do label every piece of demo data with the "Example" badge.
Do use rock people in the flat, grainy style for empty states and illustration.
Do keep the ledge on primary pressables and collapse it on press.
Do ship light and dark together; dark keeps the palette on a green-black ground.
donts: Don't add a sixth brand color or recolor the five.
Don't put an eyebrow or kicker label above a heading.
Don't use large pull quotes for emphasis.
Don't fabricate testimonials, quotes or results.
Don't put white text on green, mint, periwinkle or teal.
Don't use neutral grays; neutrals lean green.
Don't build the dark, chat-window look of AI tools or anything that reads as monitoring.
Don't put the theme switch in the landing nav; it lives in the footer.
Don't give cards or tiles a hard offset shadow; the ledge is for pressing.
